8a13b47990c5aa8ff2b7dfd503f76639f0488209.text: HUMANS VS BILLIONAIRES — Chapter 1: WILLIAM THE CONQUEROR. Three years after Hastings, the conquest is still not paid for.
8a13b47990c5aa8ff2b7dfd503f76639f0488209.speaker: Narrator

326632f5bce49509de7efe5c8fd0a1c48dd33a8e.text: The order under consideration: a scorched-earth winter campaign across Yorkshire — villages, food stores, livestock. The chroniclers will call it the Harrying of the North.
326632f5bce49509de7efe5c8fd0a1c48dd33a8e.speaker: Narrator

da03f9fe48031f8bc3c63d55f30a391630b9b34f.text: Your choices will move the RUTHLESSNESS gauge. The gauge decides what kind of ending this king deserves.
da03f9fe48031f8bc3c63d55f30a391630b9b34f.speaker: Narrator

4c3377e17f415b71f6a4c07532848de0ab35aa0c.text: The gauge in the corner is called RUTHLESSNESS. It starts at {ruthless}. Every order you give writes to it, and at Rouen it will be read back to you.
4c3377e17f415b71f6a4c07532848de0ab35aa0c.speaker: Narrator

9d3aeb583138052d1225f6a6793a64c700032786.text: Watch the RUTHLESSNESS gauge. It is not a score. It is the total this king gets buried with.
9d3aeb583138052d1225f6a6793a64c700032786.speaker: Narrator

902ea740209b94ce955fd344aa053624ecdb2cae.text: Whatever he says next, a chronicler will write it down wrong, and the shires will feel it correctly.
902ea740209b94ce955fd344aa053624ecdb2cae.speaker: Narrator

af1957df3f4ad4a458eb0ffaf19495070841ba85.text: The order goes north with the knights. No one in the hall speaks against it — counsel costs land, and land is the only currency here.
af1957df3f4ad4a458eb0ffaf19495070841ba85.speaker: Narrator

0bc898dac9da1c19311b7a411e696f6298dfce11.text: You counsel mercy. For a moment, the order is not given.
0bc898dac9da1c19311b7a411e696f6298dfce11.speaker: Narrator

839f719cd0aa537e088895c467324d21d3230fa0.text: This is the machine's logic: repression is cheaper than losing the rent. In the history we actually have, no such refusal survived the winter.
839f719cd0aa537e088895c467324d21d3230fa0.speaker: Narrator

c18b22029e44240888c4a54f001ef4d452b954e6.text: The counsel is overridden. The order goes north with the knights.
c18b22029e44240888c4a54f001ef4d452b954e6.speaker: Narrator

465da0ed97817849a915ba5823d62e096f277e64.text: Norman columns move village to village. Crops, stores, and livestock burn so that nothing can feed a rebel — or anyone else.
465da0ed97817849a915ba5823d62e096f277e64.speaker: Narrator

007c4679fd81dd19703a79ac71395001934cc792.text: You counseled mercy in the hall. The fires burn anyway. In this machine, one refusal changes the king's conscience, not the king's arithmetic.
007c4679fd81dd19703a79ac71395001934cc792.speaker: Narrator

c5257b1e9e7c6253c1a55f6f0bca0994e3f78064.text: Famine follows the fires through the winter. Orderic Vitalis — writing some fifty-five years after the event — will claim more than a hundred thousand dead; modern historians accept a catastrophe in the tens of thousands. One dissenter, Mark Hagger, argues it was no worse than other wars of the age; most scholars disagree with him.
c5257b1e9e7c6253c1a55f6f0bca0994e3f78064.speaker: Narrator

375522265fd807f96fe733dc0c5906d3ec5c3e19.text: Symeon of Durham will write that no village remained inhabited between York and Durham. Seventeen years later, the king's own survey will still mark two-thirds of Yorkshire 'vasta' — waste.
375522265fd807f96fe733dc0c5906d3ec5c3e19.speaker: Narrator

d9142ab09717ffbd2a106e1a265ac8dd6cd0e613.text: Ahead lies the next village: Aldric's. The column awaits the word.
d9142ab09717ffbd2a106e1a265ac8dd6cd0e613.speaker: Narrator

20c24a117c7b46813d42dd21088b671575cb7ea3.text: The village burns like the rest. In the spring, the survey teams will write one word next to its name: vasta.
20c24a117c7b46813d42dd21088b671575cb7ea3.speaker: Narrator

357d03347f092982ef9473bf441f00bcafa839cf.text: One village eats this winter. The chronicles will not record its name — mercy leaves a thinner paper trail than fire. But Aldric will remember.
357d03347f092982ef9473bf441f00bcafa839cf.speaker: Narrator

084f236a56f98ba7e04c6875907b1da10e715c71.text: Where the houses stood, earth is heaped into a motte. English hands dig it; a Norman keep will crown it. Some five hundred castles rise in a generation — the conquest, poured in timber and soil.
084f236a56f98ba7e04c6875907b1da10e715c71.speaker: Narrator

be743f3505f0c8a55a961e6b070e3f73167d2a6f.text: A motte is not architecture. It is a village turned inside out: the same soil, the same hands, rearranged into a thing that watches them. Some five hundred of these rise in a generation.
be743f3505f0c8a55a961e6b070e3f73167d2a6f.speaker: Narrator

882244166a371beaa433885d25ee4fcf5aad20c2.text: Not everyone starves quietly. In the fens of Ely, the water itself is a wall.
882244166a371beaa433885d25ee4fcf5aad20c2.speaker: Narrator

5a41849fb4103fdc21612d64888a1769c47691c2.text: Hereward the Wake — part fact, part legend — holds the Isle of Ely with Anglo-Saxon rebels through 1071. The chronicles remember him because resistance, too, gets written down.
5a41849fb4103fdc21612d64888a1769c47691c2.speaker: Narrator

dd9109f07e3a53af396ddbe9d3baed65e7add512.text: In Winchester the king weighs the isle. Three ways in, and every one of them is a policy.
dd9109f07e3a53af396ddbe9d3baed65e7add512.speaker: Narrator

1a7078e6c0b22fe636147d0cca9d1ae7baba6d21.text: The first causeway collapses under the weight of armored knights; the fen swallows men whole. Legend adds a hired witch on a wooden tower, and Hereward burning the whole works around her.
1a7078e6c0b22fe636147d0cca9d1ae7baba6d21.speaker: Narrator

b367ef7eb5a7b0c3fd249ff8324cd354fbd5fb9c.text: In the end it is not the causeway that takes the isle — the monks of Ely, their lands squeezed, show the king a safe path. The garrison is mutilated or imprisoned. Hereward slips into the fen-mist, and into legend.
b367ef7eb5a7b0c3fd249ff8324cd354fbd5fb9c.speaker: Narrator

e3d7c12d23b4249833aa9d261bf0f44bfe5fc4e5.text: The same logic as the Harrying, at a slower burn: cut the food, wait for the body to fail. The fen feeds its own — eels, fowl, fish — but the abbey's estates outside the water are hostage.
e3d7c12d23b4249833aa9d261bf0f44bfe5fc4e5.speaker: Narrator

eee5c8229ab89c831153ac83e1f81d83e3fc0afe.text: The monks of Ely, their revenues strangled, treat with the king and show his men the safe path in. The isle falls without a battle worth the name. Hereward slips into the mist, and into legend.
eee5c8229ab89c831153ac83e1f81d83e3fc0afe.speaker: Narrator

6b0cd0ef7ea363afa5b5d505d9a4626ec966fe74.text: Some English lords do take terms and keep their lands — at double relief and a Norman overlord. The machine prefers a paying tenant to a dead rebel, when the price is right.
6b0cd0ef7ea363afa5b5d505d9a4626ec966fe74.speaker: Narrator

764f0734246d3ecf21138d5bd7c91edb42bd8b8d.text: The monks of Ely settle first, as owners do, and show the king the causeway path. The isle passes into the survey with its rents intact. Mercy, it turns out, was also a rate.
764f0734246d3ecf21138d5bd7c91edb42bd8b8d.speaker: Narrator

e4412b2631a9c74970a82a19f76b6e9c9a253331.text: 1086. Royal commissioners fan out to survey every hide of land in England — more than thirteen thousand places, their holders, and their taxable value, so nothing escapes render.
e4412b2631a9c74970a82a19f76b6e9c9a253331.speaker: Narrator

9a46f8bbb012d0fea8852b3077744c6b5d8e6bfb.text: The survey done, William summons the landholders of England to Salisbury to swear fealty directly to him — over the heads of their own lords.
9a46f8bbb012d0fea8852b3077744c6b5d8e6bfb.speaker: Narrator

2277104db2a983350005ae13e690ed00d1881465.text: Anglo-Saxon lords are dispossessed; their tenants pay new Norman lords. Conquest has been converted into a permanent rent system — the machine this whole game is about.
2277104db2a983350005ae13e690ed00d1881465.speaker: Narrator

8a562747ae07c6c4da2381e719e78786c1fe475d.text: 9 September 1087. William lies dying near Rouen, his intestines ruptured against the saddle pommel when his horse threw him. What happens next depends on who is holding the pen.
8a562747ae07c6c4da2381e719e78786c1fe475d.speaker: Narrator

793bf9bc055f8b202ff162036af34699b5eec4ee.text: What is documented: on his deathbed he released prisoners and pardoned enemies, including his half-brother Odo. Then, Orderic reports, his attendants stripped the room and fled, leaving the body almost naked on the floor.
793bf9bc055f8b202ff162036af34699b5eec4ee.speaker: Narrator

cd244a19573c63f7cfeb9cd51d305e0023a748d4.text: ENDING: THE TOTAL. The king who burned the North is carried to the abbey he built at Caen — and even his funeral is an extraction dispute.
cd244a19573c63f7cfeb9cd51d305e0023a748d4.speaker: Narrator

0288c7d1e492189cf259ece884cec10da6283876.text: Then the bearers forced the swollen body into a stone sarcophagus cut too small. The corpse burst. Orderic records the stench driving the mourners from the church, incense helpless against it.
0288c7d1e492189cf259ece884cec10da6283876.speaker: Narrator

65adf8883013e3e326a21f6f56930af9abc22380.text: The extraction system did not die with him. It hardened into English feudalism, and its heirs are still collecting. That is why this chapter is first.
65adf8883013e3e326a21f6f56930af9abc22380.speaker: Narrator

729c612b0878ac6f8462158bbc63ced827aae430.text: Final total on the gauge: RUTHLESSNESS {ruthless}. Run it again and choose differently — the machine will show you how little that changes, and exactly how much.
729c612b0878ac6f8462158bbc63ced827aae430.speaker: Narrator

6d564c9c895ebd2de34754c7ad5e34511db0093e.text: You ended at RUTHLESSNESS {ruthless}. There is a lower number available. Whether the lower number buys anything is the question this chapter is actually asking.
6d564c9c895ebd2de34754c7ad5e34511db0093e.speaker: Narrator

7684e6d33c6ea1775e25d596fd62f5ccfed0c8f5.text: ENDING: THE SEED CORN. A quieter reckoning. The king is buried at Caen; the machine he built keeps collecting. But you were not only its instrument — and neither was everyone else.
7684e6d33c6ea1775e25d596fd62f5ccfed0c8f5.speaker: Narrator

eb0326cafc1f5944b20be87852768a517ea22967.text: In 1217, a hundred and thirty years after William's death, the Charter of the Forest will be sealed: commoners' rights to wood, pasture, and pannage restored — the first great clawback from the conquest machine.
eb0326cafc1f5944b20be87852768a517ea22967.speaker: Narrator

2610ae267b8c40cf5bfac732d0521ae6101ef579.text: Final total on the gauge: RUTHLESSNESS {ruthless}. The lowest number this chapter permits is not zero. Work out why, and you have understood the machine.
2610ae267b8c40cf5bfac732d0521ae6101ef579.speaker: Narrator

2dcb294c15d8159306d8cec8413eb061d34eb1f8.text: You ended at RUTHLESSNESS {ruthless} — and the North still burned. Play it again if you want to prove the gauge wrong. It has been tried.
2dcb294c15d8159306d8cec8413eb061d34eb1f8.speaker: Narrator

71562900c5fc293e0b8d6ae3286409b74fdd3129.text: 28 September 1066. The Norman fleet lands unopposed at Pevensey while Harold's army is far to the north.
71562900c5fc293e0b8d6ae3286409b74fdd3129.speaker: Narrator

0ccc9d20b0d37234900130b54e7ed33e2a9b0bfe.text: Who speaks? Three benches in this hall, and none of them will look at the other two.
0ccc9d20b0d37234900130b54e7ed33e2a9b0bfe.speaker: Narrator

e79ac6dfe1f514b26a820073ae82f3f6c9019cf7.text: Six mouths were within earshot of that, and they do not sit together. Pick a bench.
e79ac6dfe1f514b26a820073ae82f3f6c9019cf7.speaker: Narrator

6c5abc10c606ef54ff92809ba2f2ea2d00928e5e.text: Same event, six vantage points, three benches. Whose account do you want on the record?
6c5abc10c606ef54ff92809ba2f2ea2d00928e5e.speaker: Narrator

c9f81e1057aa4800c0c1b29dcbc47c7452371183.text: Every one of them was there, and every one of them tells it differently. That is not a flaw in the sources. That IS the sources. Start with a bench.
c9f81e1057aa4800c0c1b29dcbc47c7452371183.speaker: Narrator

1b1de7bdead45f82399cb57bcb337c1e0c281815.text: The two men who signed it. Half-brothers, whole accomplices, and each of them certain the other is the reckless one.
1b1de7bdead45f82399cb57bcb337c1e0c281815.speaker: Narrator

6f433b64e237221657e3b26eb2cf44a0db7774e2.text: The outlaw in the fen and the ploughman in the furrow. One of them is remembered. The other one fed him.
6f433b64e237221657e3b26eb2cf44a0db7774e2.speaker: Narrator

eb675e2afb280ace8fca7e76cb958a8df33934f6.text: The man who writes it down eats at the abbey the conquest paid for. The village does not, and says so at volume.
eb675e2afb280ace8fca7e76cb958a8df33934f6.speaker: Narrator

04c43469d22788232f19c82788389f8d58deeae0.text: The stumble and the answer are chroniclers' polish; the unopposed landing is fact.
04c43469d22788232f19c82788389f8d58deeae0.speaker: Narrator

4ffaab07aa4c5dcedfd02a7b9ace6366000fc10c.text: The near-contemporary Ship List records some 776 vessels pledged for the crossing — Odo's hundred among them, and his brother Mortain's hundred and twenty. The fleet was a subscription: every hull a share in land not yet taken.
4ffaab07aa4c5dcedfd02a7b9ace6366000fc10c.speaker: Narrator

27af9b8e4cf156f96f1af8cb6d9e881c1ffb7951.text: 14 October 1066. Nine hours on Senlac ridge end with Harold dead and England's door broken open.
27af9b8e4cf156f96f1af8cb6d9e881c1ffb7951.speaker: Narrator

aa3f69adc8c56419514e38796dce36cef3e0eb14.text: That the cause was Harold's oath-breaking is Norman framing; the arrow in his eye is tapestry tradition, not certainty.
aa3f69adc8c56419514e38796dce36cef3e0eb14.speaker: Narrator

3181e624467213cd79737dbf1ad25e1b680a56c6.text: Christmas Day 1066. William is crowned at Westminster while his guards, mistaking English cheers for riot, fire the surrounding houses.
3181e624467213cd79737dbf1ad25e1b680a56c6.speaker: Narrator

39cc2ae5a5d855533ae0f430b53c0162dfa5206c.text: Winter 1069. The order goes out: burn everything north of the Humber that can feed a rebel.
39cc2ae5a5d855533ae0f430b53c0162dfa5206c.speaker: Narrator

fb9a6e158b3bcbe58d4e60adf842ea6e7c95ba22.text: Winter 1069-70. The columns move village to village; the North becomes smoke.
fb9a6e158b3bcbe58d4e60adf842ea6e7c95ba22.speaker: Narrator

2dac2d011a5120a3ed119c61db7fd45b91282cb3.text: The hungry winter, 1070. Famine follows the fires; the king's own survey will still say
2dac2d011a5120a3ed119c61db7fd45b91282cb3.speaker: Narrator

52e2a55b188e6832327e8a669cc922794061f1e3.text: The deathbed confession is Orderic's composition, decades later. The famine needed no author.
52e2a55b188e6832327e8a669cc922794061f1e3.speaker: Narrator

1289949995b710d9697404d8592610c02504277d.text: 1067 to 1087. Some five hundred castles rise in a generation, many on razed streets.
1289949995b710d9697404d8592610c02504277d.speaker: Narrator

e2c3755add216734ba054d4f949d3effd4c77942.text: Around 1079. Forest law closes the woods; the New Forest is set aside for the king's deer.
e2c3755add216734ba054d4f949d3effd4c77942.speaker: Narrator

5f8a06cfc7dbc8af12360664eee358f9bca0a8c5.text: 1086. Royal commissioners survey every hide in England for the king's book — more than thirteen thousand places.
5f8a06cfc7dbc8af12360664eee358f9bca0a8c5.speaker: Narrator

52f62cd3600e12dd974ba530b09a86e7b5f541d4.text: 1 August 1086. The landholders of England swear to William directly, over their own lords' heads.
52f62cd3600e12dd974ba530b09a86e7b5f541d4.speaker: Narrator

ca04b68b0589d7151a1f131cdc17e72de17c19f1.text: The king and his enforcer-bishop. Half-brothers, whole accomplices — until the arithmetic parts them.
ca04b68b0589d7151a1f131cdc17e72de17c19f1.speaker: Narrator

5ee36a94fd594982620b25e365d5a173e38cdafb.text: Close the door and pick the argument.
5ee36a94fd594982620b25e365d5a173e38cdafb.speaker: Narrator

d5531af9d4d9e160e53e06efcf9f1e0846177569.text: Two chairs, no witnesses, no chronicler taking dictation. Which conversation?
d5531af9d4d9e160e53e06efcf9f1e0846177569.speaker: Narrator

674949e712bfdc7a58bb231dadf1ed3ba4f61907.text: Set them at each other. The record is thinnest exactly where these two talked, which is why the stage is here at all.
674949e712bfdc7a58bb231dadf1ed3ba4f61907.speaker: Narrator

6775a7470502e01977fdb90b6a490da129c9e7f3.text: These two are not finished with each other.
6775a7470502e01977fdb90b6a490da129c9e7f3.speaker: Narrator

3c9a69df861841b049c4e7f53db7058828135375.text: There is more between them than one evening holds.
3c9a69df861841b049c4e7f53db7058828135375.speaker: Narrator

77e81f865ea34e86b06343fa208a06fa58874656.text: The king and the monk who will write him. These meetings happen only on the page — Orderic was born in 1075 — and the page admits it.
77e81f865ea34e86b06343fa208a06fa58874656.speaker: Narrator

0d986ddcc14ee3ab1d9fb6033dc7956913d13879.text: The rebel and the ploughman. One wants recruits; the other wants a harvest.
0d986ddcc14ee3ab1d9fb6033dc7956913d13879.speaker: Narrator

6eabe6ce903c70cee7f3b03c7b566cc863e8ba4b.text: The patron and the scribe. One commissions the story; the other keeps writing the wrong one.
6eabe6ce903c70cee7f3b03c7b566cc863e8ba4b.speaker: Narrator

dcd24af8ea4c0a3cfa216781e82be55c393df3e1.text: The king and the outlaw. No chronicle records them meeting — so this stage does what chronicles do, and invents carefully.
dcd24af8ea4c0a3cfa216781e82be55c393df3e1.speaker: Narrator

1b509ad6942f5108d4657dc9cde741d7fe98c30f.text: The ploughman and his neighbors. Every royal policy ends here, as an argument at the moot.
1b509ad6942f5108d4657dc9cde741d7fe98c30f.speaker: Narrator

8dbc205b7a3f237cb6372ba4c139f76f7759fd98.text: The survey's deepest function, historians note, was exactly this: fixing what the king's own barons owed him. Extraction disciplines its middlemen first.
8dbc205b7a3f237cb6372ba4c139f76f7759fd98.speaker: Narrator

39c5a33ef95d571f54a5b88ccca5989cb7ac89ff.text: It took four and a half centuries, but a king did the sums. The dissolution of the monasteries was Domesday's logic finally applied to Domesday's biggest winner.
39c5a33ef95d571f54a5b88ccca5989cb7ac89ff.speaker: Narrator

b627b762a35cd1639e0b676cd09abdcd5e568343.text: 1082. Odo — regent, richest man in England after the king — is caught recruiting knights for a private venture in Italy. Some said he meant to buy the papacy itself.
b627b762a35cd1639e0b676cd09abdcd5e568343.speaker: Narrator

6c6284ec300dc97795d523fcfcac662fe46e52ca.text: The lawyer's trick is reported by the chroniclers. Domesday values the arrested earl's lands at some £3,000 across twenty-two counties — second only to the king's. Odo sat imprisoned at Rouen until William, dying, pardoned him — the machine forgiving its own component.
6c6284ec300dc97795d523fcfcac662fe46e52ca.speaker: Narrator

a37ee9db3c8fc52c36df98c064dba3eddb4ea766.text: The great geld of 1085 and the Domesday inquest were twin instruments: the emergency tax, then the machine to make every future tax inescapable.
a37ee9db3c8fc52c36df98c064dba3eddb4ea766.speaker: Narrator

e408892f3cc12ef888515700f9c59f78cdd8ef2c.text: Castle-work was among the burdens the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle listed bitterly under this reign: the conquered digging the conquest in deeper, at their own charge.
e408892f3cc12ef888515700f9c59f78cdd8ef2c.speaker: Narrator

595ce87f13d1e20d9e4be37359a91f834f8a3e7d.text: September 1087. The dying king has pardoned nearly everyone — except, for days, one name.
595ce87f13d1e20d9e4be37359a91f834f8a3e7d.speaker: Narrator

ee3fcfdd9fbf39568e6e3b6173e1920cefdf8246.text: He did pardon him — documented, unlike the speeches. And Odo did trouble his sons: within a year he led the rebellion of 1088 against William Rufus. The wound knew itself.
ee3fcfdd9fbf39568e6e3b6173e1920cefdf8246.speaker: Narrator

dfdd11d15e3dc234cc1ca0c587385d7e15e9e297.text: Understand the device before it speaks: Orderic Vitalis was born in 1075, nine years after Hastings. He never stood before this king. Every meeting here happens where all their meetings happened — on the page.
dfdd11d15e3dc234cc1ca0c587385d7e15e9e297.speaker: Narrator

9e0ee26746bfe76a1ea260dbcd44d2d22a579f07.text: Orderic wrote this some fifty-five years after the fires. The historians' consensus runs tens of thousands against his 100,000; Mark Hagger dissents that the Harrying was no worse than other conflicts of the age, and most of his colleagues dissent from the dissent. No historian runs it to zero.
9e0ee26746bfe76a1ea260dbcd44d2d22a579f07.speaker: Narrator

326a7ec082396cf1f1f8ab0ef76b24876d1fee79.text: The rebellion and the ploughman: allies against the machine, and not quite allies about what should replace it. This argument is older than both of them, and outlived both.
326a7ec082396cf1f1f8ab0ef76b24876d1fee79.speaker: Narrator

0e33e3cd3355a7f7c2741bce7bf952dae4533d07.text: The fen as sanctuary is well-attested; its limits equally so. Every resistance is also a ration.
0e33e3cd3355a7f7c2741bce7bf952dae4533d07.speaker: Narrator

c73fac8a6773ac6879a17de3f380b233d51b2343.text: The Bayeux Tapestry's Norman program and its ambiguous English-made margins are both real, and art historians still argue over what the borders mutter.
c73fac8a6773ac6879a17de3f380b233d51b2343.speaker: Narrator

0d510d0a7ac016efb4c9d8c88823e4e433a8ac26.text: Halley's Comet did appear in spring 1066; every party read it as an omen against the other. Omens are the medieval word for editorial.
0d510d0a7ac016efb4c9d8c88823e4e433a8ac26.speaker: Narrator

dd916b278d81d601dc8653a4f4e112d82f866b98.text: Flag this plainly: no chronicle records William and Hereward ever meeting. What follows is counterfactual — the conversation the sources leave a hole shaped like.
dd916b278d81d601dc8653a4f4e112d82f866b98.speaker: Narrator

cc202dad81ea3184c05f069922cb676e702be2c5.text: Counterfactual, again — though this one nearly happened: some traditions say Hereward eventually made peace and held land under William. The chroniclers disagree; the stage may choose.
cc202dad81ea3184c05f069922cb676e702be2c5.speaker: Narrator

d206e6dc3d0931a7eb565a67680e4762bbe70c64.text: A third invented meeting: two theories of England, given one stage.
d206e6dc3d0931a7eb565a67680e4762bbe70c64.speaker: Narrator

368d2699506e521c80c4b1b5351417b4b3abdd38.text: Forest law was, among other things, the crown's attempt to conquer the between-places. It manufactured outlaws for two centuries, and then it manufactured Robin Hood.
368d2699506e521c80c4b1b5351417b4b3abdd38.speaker: Narrator

39619d41d1cf87456f536b8f77a0fe566d0bda2f.text: Last invention: both men dead, arguing over the estate that neither can hold — memory.
39619d41d1cf87456f536b8f77a0fe566d0bda2f.speaker: Narrator

fc0461884e30868e1764f1d008b47774953d8758.text: No chronicle records this parish or this floor. Chronicles record what lords do. What villages did under their fonts is exactly the kind of fact that survives as absence — and as the villages that, somehow, sowed in spring.
fc0461884e30868e1764f1d008b47774953d8758.speaker: Narrator

53eccb9b4608936ffee77eafbcf7352a8b93ee2b.text: This quiet trespass, multiplied by every forest village for a century and a half, is what the Charter of the Forest finally wrote back into law in 1217. First the practice, then the right.
53eccb9b4608936ffee77eafbcf7352a8b93ee2b.speaker: Narrator

a3115743ae227ea8da915e1a23566d7fef554968.text: Put two of them in a room and close the door. Where the chronicles record no such room, the stage says so out loud.
a3115743ae227ea8da915e1a23566d7fef554968.speaker: Narrator

ad68a30a9d09ce5db0b31f79d85092770a107468.text: History is mostly one voice at a time, edited. Put two in a room and the edits start arguing with each other. Where no such room existed, this stage admits it in the first line.
ad68a30a9d09ce5db0b31f79d85092770a107468.speaker: Narrator

0b2937652ac7704a7be5b751c7917a9958e37223.text: Six pairings. Some of these meetings are documented, some are counterfactual, and every counterfactual one flags itself before it opens its mouth. That is the house rule.
0b2937652ac7704a7be5b751c7917a9958e37223.speaker: Narrator

59b9a42032aec9445006b24d4ca7a6e16b9eaa68.text: Two rooms where the conquerors argue with the conquerors. Nobody in either room speaks English, and nobody in either room thinks that is a problem.
59b9a42032aec9445006b24d4ca7a6e16b9eaa68.speaker: Narrator

dc2c6826bde6532d23b0b51fbea2312fa24314dd.text: Two rooms that never existed. One puts the king in front of the monk who will damn him; one puts him in front of the outlaw he never caught. Both flag themselves in the first line.
dc2c6826bde6532d23b0b51fbea2312fa24314dd.speaker: Narrator

66b72c501db8969bf73717ec451667da27419e6c.text: Two rooms with no Normans in them at all. This is where the conquest gets argued about by the people it actually happened to.
66b72c501db8969bf73717ec451667da27419e6c.speaker: Narrator

584af838bceff49aae6abb2349e1be21986eefec.text: That night there were hundreds of such roads. The chronicles compress them into a sentence; the sentence took all winter to walk.
584af838bceff49aae6abb2349e1be21986eefec.speaker: Narrator

a38e8f26b7d91117e42c4391e1fc8c409a4377b9.text: Famine's second year is crueler than its first: the first eats the food, the second eats the future. That is what burning seed corn buys.
a38e8f26b7d91117e42c4391e1fc8c409a4377b9.speaker: Narrator

8ea1f4f0195460322bce91fe6962e9268e7f9a45.text: The Harrying's last casualty was the memory of alternatives. When the survey's grandchildren paid their dues, they paid them as the order of nature.
8ea1f4f0195460322bce91fe6962e9268e7f9a45.speaker: Narrator

cd405fda4cc55b8cc0f31a9455f33803ee10e15b.text: Complicity by silence is the machine's cheapest component. It was fully staffed that night.
cd405fda4cc55b8cc0f31a9455f33803ee10e15b.speaker: Narrator

141f8f03cb598ac666b617bc5e55bf8940c6e301.text: The regime's own arithmetic condemned the policy sooner than its conscience did. Waste pays no rent — the survey would spend pages proving it.
141f8f03cb598ac666b617bc5e55bf8940c6e301.speaker: Narrator

4afbe8e81353839af371951ba5b234227136f153.text: Every extraction system learns this accounting: atrocity is a loss on every page except the one that matters to power. Keep your eye on which page they balance.
4afbe8e81353839af371951ba5b234227136f153.speaker: Narrator

cf6bc5034d16f1f96cfcd13f7e27414ee5b4f15d.text: It did. What is assessed is owned differently forever after. The village learned in one afternoon what economists would need eight centuries to phrase.
cf6bc5034d16f1f96cfcd13f7e27414ee5b4f15d.speaker: Narrator

fd81d0115e92cbaa44c1d881182fcbd2123bf337.text: A fixed assessment converts every bad harvest into debt. The book's permanence — its whole point — is precisely what made it merciless.
fd81d0115e92cbaa44c1d881182fcbd2123bf337.speaker: Narrator

63d40c420b4b387b62efffbc3ea377ae35b04868.text: Domesday's entries were cited in English courts into the twentieth century. The boy's morning lasted, by conservative count, eight hundred years.
63d40c420b4b387b62efffbc3ea377ae35b04868.speaker: Narrator

8812352a3c4c53cd6d7391a52c71c03cb06613d5.text: The sworn local juries are documented procedure. Extraction that co-signs its subjects is extraction that plans to last.
8812352a3c4c53cd6d7391a52c71c03cb06613d5.speaker: Narrator

7a90d9863db90b2d190b3481622b84e069fe6e90.text: Great Domesday was largely written by a single scribe, and work continued around the king's death. Systems outlive the appetites that commission them — that is what makes them systems.
7a90d9863db90b2d190b3481622b84e069fe6e90.speaker: Narrator

70b78281004a25fbd870a8a1f53b6acd88cbd865.text: By the 1170s the English themselves called it Domesday — judgment day — 'because its decisions, like those of the Last Judgement, are unalterable.' The nickname is the review.
70b78281004a25fbd870a8a1f53b6acd88cbd865.speaker: Narrator

5305bf290058d681bfdff85efa764e75741bdda0.text: Forest law criminalized custom itself — firewood, pannage, the hare in the pot. It is the purest case in the whole chapter: nothing was taken except the right to use.
5305bf290058d681bfdff85efa764e75741bdda0.speaker: Narrator

00240b33a541b4de1873ae069143803466bebf90.text: The court's penalties — mutilation in the harshest tellings, chronicler-reported — did the advertising. The dusk-paths did the resisting. Both institutions ran for a century and a half.
00240b33a541b4de1873ae069143803466bebf90.speaker: Narrator

7270d7c1c88705e196aa78397637a5611a032312.text: William Rufus died by arrow in the New Forest in 1100 — accident by every sober account, judgment by every village one. When a law manufactures outlaws, it also manufactures the audience for that whisper.
7270d7c1c88705e196aa78397637a5611a032312.speaker: Narrator

e8924b1b211760dda696b4c08d724368574487ed.text: The royal forest was a Norman legal invention on English ground: jurisdiction as property. It is rent abstracted one full turn further than land itself.
e8924b1b211760dda696b4c08d724368574487ed.speaker: Narrator

8cd8e6811db9628f0e8b939241c6ae4b2bd5f9e5.text: He understood commons better than the commoners' own advocates: every use-right is a leak in the rent. Forest law was the caulking.
8cd8e6811db9628f0e8b939241c6ae4b2bd5f9e5.speaker: Narrator

1eea30b828f8900fa81d456716213424ae01a28f.text: The Chronicle's verse obituary is real and unsparing: the deer-line, the castles, the geld. A century of forest misery later, the Charter of 1217 began prying the fence back open.
1eea30b828f8900fa81d456716213424ae01a28f.speaker: Narrator

70a802599f794c544b211c1edc9ef2d159058d50.text: The Salisbury oath cut across the feudal chain — vassal's vassal bound directly to the crown. It is the constitutional moment of the whole machine: no ground, and now no allegiance, outside the system.
70a802599f794c544b211c1edc9ef2d159058d50.speaker: Narrator

25ffec52d90946a4a47955bccd07836d23b04368.text: The reservation of fealty to the king became standard in homage. Conquest had finished converting itself into boilerplate — the most durable material known to power.
25ffec52d90946a4a47955bccd07836d23b04368.speaker: Narrator

a875178ce68aa8533a857eccc45c874115258d6d.text: Tenures traceable to the Conquest settlement structured English landholding for centuries; its doctrine — all land held of the Crown — remains the formal root of English land law today. Forever was only barely an exaggeration.
a875178ce68aa8533a857eccc45c874115258d6d.speaker: Narrator

79c018a071fff1c6cb3d73607519ee82f04459cd.text: For the plough, the oath changed nothing that day — which is itself the finding. Constitutional revolutions at the top arrive at the bottom as continuity.
79c018a071fff1c6cb3d73607519ee82f04459cd.speaker: Narrator

5e50f078e195fff12617b456a415c5ca75432dd9.text: Interchangeable lordship is the oath's deepest gift to extraction: the system no longer depends on any particular extractor. George would recognize it instantly — the rent survives every landlord.
5e50f078e195fff12617b456a415c5ca75432dd9.speaker: Narrator

a59d46e5408346e308bacaecb4afda518d743e3e.text: Post-Conquest law hardened many free English smallholders toward villeinage — free in name, bound in obligation. The chapter's thesis in one household: the margin did not close by decree; it closed by arithmetic.
a59d46e5408346e308bacaecb4afda518d743e3e.speaker: Narrator

164d8f0d9a516dff089d89a3d1de09a981b55689.text: An order is an evening's work. What it ordered goes on for generations. Four policies, two vantage points each: that night, a season later, a generation later.
164d8f0d9a516dff089d89a3d1de09a981b55689.speaker: Narrator

de1ce103b0b7ac074fefb100b5d4deced6bb2054.text: Policy is fast. Consequence is slow. Four orders, followed down three time-scales apiece — the night it happened, the season it bit, the generation that could no longer imagine otherwise.
de1ce103b0b7ac074fefb100b5d4deced6bb2054.speaker: Narrator

9bbfad46487867b644409345a606a654befa673f.text: The chronicles give you the evening the order was signed. They almost never give you the spring. Here are the springs.
9bbfad46487867b644409345a606a654befa673f.speaker: Narrator

5f6cbcc79082fb90f56df830e73d3e1a7969f7ad.text: One winter's order. Follow it from the man whose barn went up, or from the man who added the column afterward and found the arithmetic acceptable.
5f6cbcc79082fb90f56df830e73d3e1a7969f7ad.speaker: Narrator

cdc60d2261fcd8947d1a302f225f57ca1a9625e2.text: A survey is an evening's work for the clerk and a permanent condition for the vill. Two vantage points: the assessed, and the record.
cdc60d2261fcd8947d1a302f225f57ca1a9625e2.speaker: Narrator

30d29ba7c00533879243910675347aa58167ee88.text: Two more orders with very long tails: a forest fenced against the people living in it, and a field full of men swearing to one man forever.
30d29ba7c00533879243910675347aa58167ee88.speaker: Narrator

8a788c4224dab579c730a59dff99eecf4844b6d6.text: Deer become the king's deer, and a man who has hunted that wood his whole life becomes a poacher without moving. Two vantage points.
8a788c4224dab579c730a59dff99eecf4844b6d6.speaker: Narrator

504a479fac66137399e28d93e78d27c244b11218.text: Every landholder in England, in one field, swearing past his own lord straight to the king. Two vantage points: the crown, and the ground it is standing on.
504a479fac66137399e28d93e78d27c244b11218.speaker: Narrator

b68121770ca2da9fb53633db5fe2f396ca46da16.text: 1075. The Revolt of the Earls — the last serious rising of the reign, and it is not English at all. It is hatched by William's OWN earls, at a wedding.
b68121770ca2da9fb53633db5fe2f396ca46da16.speaker: Narrator

b3fe9e62b64dfcc807ca90f0076558164402a361.text: Greed inside the machine proved as combustible as grievance outside it. The revolt collapsed within months — the interesting part is what happened to each conspirator.
b3fe9e62b64dfcc807ca90f0076558164402a361.speaker: Narrator

d53919bf7abf937176c65f3cf8412719d6d99528.text: The revolt is crushed while William is still in Normandy — the system suppressing a rising without its king, which is its own grim milestone. Then the sentencing.
d53919bf7abf937176c65f3cf8412719d6d99528.speaker: Narrator

d162fbcaddd758141401ae79f3501c846b0fa01c.text: The Danish fleet that came for the 1069 rising winters in the Humber — the rebels' great hope, the invasion that could reopen everything. William does not fight it.
d162fbcaddd758141401ae79f3501c846b0fa01c.speaker: Narrator

80a86846aca3eee8f9569e2fd0b354ba3bd89f8f.text: The Danes took the Danegeld and sailed, as Danes had before and would again. The North's last outside hope left with them — bought, not beaten.
80a86846aca3eee8f9569e2fd0b354ba3bd89f8f.speaker: Narrator

3e2a05c6e7c3ff98303ceaf481e97c3a94008b87.text: 1085. Cnut IV of Denmark assembles a great fleet to invade England. William's response is the largest army ever brought into the kingdom — of mercenaries.
3e2a05c6e7c3ff98303ceaf481e97c3a94008b87.speaker: Narrator

36b2a44c229fa8d1da50c4a2e380d3f03fb0094d.text: The Chronicle links the great host of 1085 and the deep speech at Gloucester that launched Domesday. The invasion never came; the invoice became permanent. Emergencies are how machines acquire new organs.
36b2a44c229fa8d1da50c4a2e380d3f03fb0094d.speaker: Narrator

89237eea06463ab31c97e48ff2e8507847a67f37.text: The heavy geld of 1084 at six shillings the hide is on the record; the survey followed within two years. Tax first, then build the instrument that perfects the tax: the sequence is the signature of the machine.
89237eea06463ab31c97e48ff2e8507847a67f37.speaker: Narrator

4a40bf65c81dd43b70719089a24bb24f66c03023.text: How did the unassailable isle fall? Not to the causeway. The abbey of Ely held rich estates OUTSIDE the fens — and the king quietly took possession of every one.
4a40bf65c81dd43b70719089a24bb24f66c03023.speaker: Narrator

f2a8aacf6b4bcbaec1263cc0a9468b75eb5c4a43.text: Property held hostage beat an impregnable position. Note the mechanism — it is the same one that ends most resistance in this game: not defeat. Foreclosure.
f2a8aacf6b4bcbaec1263cc0a9468b75eb5c4a43.speaker: Narrator

db519f014990cf9b956612a1969434425842395c.text: The king's men cross by the shown path. The isle that could not be stormed is simply walked into. Then the sentences.
db519f014990cf9b956612a1969434425842395c.speaker: Narrator

0f86ac4a75eb385a7f81179165ad09e2856b41dd.text: The mutilation of the Ely garrison is chronicle-reported; Hereward's end is genuinely unknown. Both facts have been doing their separate work ever since.
0f86ac4a75eb385a7f81179165ad09e2856b41dd.speaker: Narrator

26ec7aa69b0efade25db30ba96ccd067db4902a7.text: Lammas Day, 1086. The Chronicle's own words: there came to him 'all the land-holding men of any account throughout England, whosesoever men they were.' Whosesoever men they were — the clause that changed the constitution.
26ec7aa69b0efade25db30ba96ccd067db4902a7.speaker: Narrator

30f0f1a1a94d4600d30ec82da670a197fc139ea8.text: Historians pair the oath with Domesday as the Conquest's administrative consummation: first know exactly what every man holds, then bind every holder directly to the crown. The machine's two hands, closing.
30f0f1a1a94d4600d30ec82da670a197fc139ea8.speaker: Narrator

784ec0ab25545e64d527054f97c6b6f00f64bc6e.text: Foreshadow, thirteen years past the king's death. His son William Rufus, hunting in the New Forest his father emptied by law, takes an arrow through the chest. His companions abandon the body; a charcoal-burner carts it to Winchester.
784ec0ab25545e64d527054f97c6b6f00f64bc6e.speaker: Narrator

7e90353fad533ca656b69da575474d54b1fba348.text: The Rufus death is fact; the meaning is folklore — and the folklore is data. When a legal system is hated enough, even its accidents get entered on the other side of the ledger.
7e90353fad533ca656b69da575474d54b1fba348.speaker: Narrator

ea06bfce2dce962ab81285780eb317b70f570760.text: The funeral at Caen, and the moment the whole chapter has been arguing toward. As the body is borne to the grave, a man steps out of the crowd and stops the rite.
ea06bfce2dce962ab81285780eb317b70f570760.speaker: Narrator

c119fdb969e1dd4a53d013bd211216b33f96ff95.text: Orderic and the other chroniclers report the scene in detail. Whatever they embellished, the shape is perfect beyond invention: the machine's founder could not enter the ground until the ground was paid for.
c119fdb969e1dd4a53d013bd211216b33f96ff95.speaker: Narrator

3ae24480a87c57df1eb6c08f297f30f11293e1a9.text: The looted deathbed, the graveside extortion, the coffin that would not fit: the chroniclers assembled William's ending into the medieval world's most complete parable of extraction. This game did not have to invent its moral. 1087 wrote it first.
3ae24480a87c57df1eb6c08f297f30f11293e1a9.speaker: Narrator

2847fc1f19220505d9ce48ab1cd63c999c9fa0d5.text: The year the king dies, an English monk writes his obituary in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle — in verse, in English, for English readers. It is the conquered's considered review of the Conqueror.
2847fc1f19220505d9ce48ab1cd63c999c9fa0d5.speaker: Narrator

1b6e354c7be350993aa67a3903fe42d2f1e7ff31.text: The Peterborough Chronicle's verdict, written under Norman rule by men with everything to lose, survived nine centuries. Every regime learns it eventually: you can dispossess the literate, but they file a report.
1b6e354c7be350993aa67a3903fe42d2f1e7ff31.speaker: Narrator

4bb4a4703bf9885921b501f4b42ea50ece3b7add.text: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle ran to 1154 — the longest act of documentary resistance in this whole game, and the direct ancestor of every witness, chronicler, and whistleblower in the chapters that follow. The machine builds its book. Someone always builds the other one.
4bb4a4703bf9885921b501f4b42ea50ece3b7add.speaker: Narrator

a227e2708f39613455048ab9972ca913f7ade9e0.text: One loose end the machine handled with strange gentleness: Edgar Aetheling, last male heir of the House of Wessex — the boy the North rose for in 1069, the rightful king by English blood.
a227e2708f39613455048ab9972ca913f7ade9e0.speaker: Narrator

2cd479690c8cd39097beae56152dad657031dfea.text: Edgar outlived William by nearly forty years, on the pension, in the record — the revolution that was never crushed because it was successfully SALARIED.
2cd479690c8cd39097beae56152dad657031dfea.speaker: Narrator

ee72fe5f5a88b9bf1b33463b06ea3013bbbf1a29.text: Before a single ship is built, the enterprise acquires its most valuable cargo: a consecrated banner from Pope Alexander II. Watch the two meters this one object moves.
ee72fe5f5a88b9bf1b33463b06ea3013bbbf1a29.speaker: Narrator

f09eacecdbff954cfddb956f0d9274e494a50fe3.text: In the machine's terms: PRESTIGE up, REGULATION down — the referee blessed the acquisition before it happened. Moral cover is the cheapest insurance extraction ever buys. (The record wobbles: some scholars argue the banner was formally conferred only at Winchester, c.1070 — the receipt possibly backdated.)
f09eacecdbff954cfddb956f0d9274e494a50fe3.speaker: Narrator

bd7309040c0f0d5de29e836e63b7744df60ab1da.text: Lillebonne, January 1066. The barons of Normandy balk: no feudal duty obliges them to cross a sea. So William makes them an offer that is the Georgist seed of this whole chapter.
bd7309040c0f0d5de29e836e63b7744df60ab1da.speaker: Narrator

9944757cba1a963b24ccf5c71912a2cf67cf7e10.text: They did. Hold the sequence in view, because every chapter of this game repeats it: conquest converted into property, property into rent, rent into perpetuity. The swords were the down payment; England's fields were the dividend; the payout schedule was FOREVER.
9944757cba1a963b24ccf5c71912a2cf67cf7e10.speaker: Narrator

fd5f446c335cb8feae406ef340d3c8b5dbc79cdd.text: The fleet gathers at the mouth of the Dives by mid-August — and the wind refuses. For about a month the greatest speculation of the century sits at anchor, eating itself.
fd5f446c335cb8feae406ef340d3c8b5dbc79cdd.speaker: Narrator

dbad767671e06ecac54aac0f1c09408100c21989.text: The wind turned at Michaelmas; the fleet crossed the night of 27-28 September and landed unopposed. Wace later counted 696 ships — chroniclers audit each other too. But the shape is exact: England was not just invaded. It was UNDERWRITTEN.
dbad767671e06ecac54aac0f1c09408100c21989.speaker: Narrator

12bf201603b29be4b5729de7ff8d3ae69fc5f922.text: FLAG THIS SCENE BEFORE IT PLAYS: everything in it is Norman testimony. No English source corroborates the oath. This is the story the conquest told to license itself.
12bf201603b29be4b5729de7ff8d3ae69fc5f922.speaker: Narrator

e5b176b09a9a8fcae5a38ef3710d976a9fb67681.text: The oath was argued at Rome by Lanfranc and became the banner, the invasion's license. Whether it happened — and what Harold thought he swore, under what duress — the sources cannot say. The machine did not need it true. It needed it TOLD.
e5b176b09a9a8fcae5a38ef3710d976a9fb67681.speaker: Narrator

03dc3e8364459667eb855cf14e6663ba2f99b24e.text: Christmas Day, 1066. Ealdred, Archbishop of York — who crowned Harold in January — now crowns William in December. The rite is asked in two languages.
03dc3e8364459667eb855cf14e6663ba2f99b24e.speaker: Narrator

7dfea782ec5c1f37ca2e195b1318f80a6d0380d6.text: Reported by Orderic, writing later — but the shape is the reign in miniature: consent, illegible to the enforcers, answered with fire; and at the center of the smoke, an anointed king shaking. He was crowned by a machine that could not tell cheering from rebellion, and never learned to.
7dfea782ec5c1f37ca2e195b1318f80a6d0380d6.speaker: Narrator

267f264e5ca7a59d9b4dd5cda8924d81ba2c7291.text: Consider the defendant's portfolio. Bishop of Bayeux. Earl of Kent. One hundred ships at the crossing. Lands Domesday will value near £3,000 across twenty-two counties — second only to the king. And, most likely, the patron who commissioned the Bayeux Tapestry itself.
267f264e5ca7a59d9b4dd5cda8924d81ba2c7291.speaker: Narrator

ae5f62c14a8617ac1cfc74d5fc932cca8f2fe15f.text: Arrest, trial, prison at Rouen — the sentence the dying king reluctantly lifted. Odo died in 1097 en route to Crusade. Mark the lesson every chapter of this game repeats: the machine forgives its enemies before its auditors. Extraction can absorb any crime except skimming.
ae5f62c14a8617ac1cfc74d5fc932cca8f2fe15f.speaker: Narrator

79de7f88dfa2168a0c0eaee54cb9b870821abc0f.text: Open the book to the winners' pages. Read what each man took — and, where the record kept it, whose it was.
79de7f88dfa2168a0c0eaee54cb9b870821abc0f.speaker: Narrator

f92eee951a68fb2aeb0ffe8e36948e5a931f5deb.text: Every line of the ledger has an erased name under it. Domesday is a palimpsest: a conquest written over a country, in the neatest hand in Europe. And the ink is not dry yet — turn the page nine hundred years.
f92eee951a68fb2aeb0ffe8e36948e5a931f5deb.speaker: Narrator

5a36d27bac90ac75b6365a789a9e8600d5dd3b79.text: Around 1070 the Church presents the victors with a bill. The Penitential Ordinance of Ermenfrid of Sion prices the conquest, sin by sin — read the tariff.
5a36d27bac90ac75b6365a789a9e8600d5dd3b79.speaker: Narrator

79b8b804f1eab51c18f6e3b88375c0c44da10c5a.text: A moral system that prices every sin and exempts the principal shareholder is not a conscience — it is a subsidiary. The Church billed the workforce and comped the owner. Now watch what the owner built with the savings.
79b8b804f1eab51c18f6e3b88375c0c44da10c5a.speaker: Narrator

b820f2445e7c7afb928fcce182b3f8700164e1d9.text: Tally the insulation: a banner from the Pope, a penance that exempted the principal, an abbey on the enemy's grave, a court history for the record. Prestige is not the machine's decoration. It is the machine's ARMOR — and it was itemized.
b820f2445e7c7afb928fcce182b3f8700164e1d9.speaker: Narrator

f926188e3a4c1c719daf0fb8e216444241fbfc0e.text: One voice ran through every legal joint of the conquest: Lanfranc of Bec — the lawyer who argued William's case at Rome, then came to collect the fee.
f926188e3a4c1c719daf0fb8e216444241fbfc0e.speaker: Narrator

67d7a51481677f7f0bedb27b970eb3b4cce4283e.text: January 1066: Ealdred of York crowns Harold Godwinson. December 1066: the same hands, the same rite, crown William. One year, two kings, one archbishop.
67d7a51481677f7f0bedb27b970eb3b4cce4283e.speaker: Narrator

66febe3fb976c809eb96c319534540059195169f.text: The institution survives every king it crowns; that is its power and its alibi. Ealdred's bargain — legitimacy in exchange for promises — is the oldest trade in this game. The promises were spent by spring. The legitimacy is still earning.
66febe3fb976c809eb96c319534540059195169f.speaker: Narrator

933148282025ffc81fb5dec18ee25022f839deac.text: Last entry in the Chronicle, and the spine of the whole game, made explicit. The question is simple: did the extraction of 1066 ever actually STOP?
933148282025ffc81fb5dec18ee25022f839deac.speaker: Narrator

1a785e6a4b7c5c98d986a1feb379b62e04a267c9.text: Conquest became property; property became rent; rent became a rich list with the conquest's surnames on it. That is why this chapter is first, and why Henry George haunts every one that follows: the fire went out in 1070. The RENT is being collected this morning.
1a785e6a4b7c5c98d986a1feb379b62e04a267c9.speaker: Narrator

caea79bd9b6f979e2c224ebbfec7016f544a0282.text: The research holds more than the main stage could carry: the papal banner and the land-for-swords bargain, the windbound fleet, the coronation fire, the earls' revolt, the barons' ledger, the funeral — and the rent still being collected this morning. Orderic keeps the index.
caea79bd9b6f979e2c224ebbfec7016f544a0282.speaker: Narrator

68d62c25b08931395884595010076da5edab7f41.text: The art in this chapter is a forgery of something real. Here is the real thing: seventy metres of embroidered linen, made by English hands within living memory of the conquest, telling the conquerors' side of it.
68d62c25b08931395884595010076da5edab7f41.speaker: Narrator

7a9af514de4d3053c748c54447ffd2feaab01680.text: One object survives the whole of Chapter One: a strip of linen half a metre tall and seventy long, with the invasion sewn onto it in coloured wool. It is the closest thing 1066 has to a camera.
7a9af514de4d3053c748c54447ffd2feaab01680.speaker: Narrator

ab4bcae6db0b1acb99da34b2f34a1b357654d3b6.text: Read it as this game reads everything else — as a document with an owner. Somebody paid for it, somebody stitched it, and those were not the same people.
ab4bcae6db0b1acb99da34b2f34a1b357654d3b6.speaker: Narrator

d5216205596aef69a7f888b82ea91d5c9e1085e4.text: Start with the thing itself, because almost everything people say about it is wrong at the first word. It is not a tapestry. A tapestry is woven — the picture IS the cloth. This is embroidery: wool worked with a needle onto linen that was already there.
d5216205596aef69a7f888b82ea91d5c9e1085e4.speaker: Narrator

294c8e4c679012108d519fff7402d7a3464618f8.text: Nine strips of bleached linen, seamed together so cleanly the joins hide inside the pictures. Near seventy metres end to end, about fifty centimetres tall. The usual count gives some six hundred people, two hundred horses, forty-one ships, and about fifty-eight lines of Latin — and the counts differ depending on who is counting.
294c8e4c679012108d519fff7402d7a3464618f8.speaker: Narrator

77f8d5833818d8701f63c94e5fbfd91e1a44ad49.text: Hold what that means. Within a decade or two of Hastings, English women — the conquered, in a conquered county, working for the conqueror's half-brother — sewed the conquest of England, in the conquerors' Latin, at their own speed, with their own fingers.
77f8d5833818d8701f63c94e5fbfd91e1a44ad49.speaker: Narrator

b58d5b9a1f2eba58c9e436c5ac3279da32d97249.text: This is the part the chapter's own pictures are stealing from, so it is worth a minute.
b58d5b9a1f2eba58c9e436c5ac3279da32d97249.speaker: Narrator

b85f4074ccb5ce41da258d2d871372ddec480ae3.text: One flag before the clips. Sections of the cloth were repaired and restitched in the nineteenth century, and at least one famous detail may have been changed in the repairing. That matters shortly.
b85f4074ccb5ce41da258d2d871372ddec480ae3.speaker: Narrator

5ce6bba178bbddcdbc44f8034da3e37588911577.text: Clip one. Six men on the cloth, shoulder to shoulder, every one of them pointing up at the same thing, and four words stitched over their heads: ISTI MIRANT STELLA. These men wonder at the star.
5ce6bba178bbddcdbc44f8034da3e37588911577.speaker: Narrator

18511a96b22dfef2f516d590b4c50a0a2de8bc77.text: Halley's Comet, spring 1066 — the same comet, on the same orbit, that came back in 1910 and 1986 and will come back in 2061. On the cloth it hangs over the new king like a thrown stone that has not landed yet.
18511a96b22dfef2f516d590b4c50a0a2de8bc77.speaker: Narrator

a18e2d213479af47c4b64bcbc3d86b26f90ffcb0.text: It became one. That is the whole use of an omen: it moves the conquest out of the column marked THEFT and into the column marked SCHEDULE. Heaven signed off in April; the invoice arrives in October.
a18e2d213479af47c4b64bcbc3d86b26f90ffcb0.speaker: Narrator

baef3828ddec3f1db7aae2275199b472186c6514.text: Clip two, and it is the least famous and the most useful stretch on the whole cloth: HERE DUKE WILLIAM ORDERED SHIPS TO BE BUILT.
baef3828ddec3f1db7aae2275199b472186c6514.speaker: Narrator

e000a5e3cccc27b3a96b7965966c45c8f3e8ab34.text: Then the sequence, in order, as any shipwright would tell it: men fell the trees with axes. Men shape the trunks with adzes. Hulls take shape on trestles. Ropes drag them to the water. Then the loading — mail-shirts slung on poles between two men, helmets, spear-bundles, a cask of wine, and horses walked up the planks.
e000a5e3cccc27b3a96b7965966c45c8f3e8ab34.speaker: Narrator

9f81d2cf8800f23200cac409718423c1f5e7658f.text: The Tapestry is the conquest's own advertisement, and it advertises the supply chain: fell, build, load, land, forage, feast. The fighting is the last quarter. The first three-quarters are LOGISTICS — which is where every conquest in this game actually happens.
9f81d2cf8800f23200cac409718423c1f5e7658f.speaker: Narrator

b161795b0470578ec4d375341a2f109e111c8296.text: Clip three. Run a strip above the story and a strip below it, and fill both with animals: lions, griffins, camels, peacocks, dogs, birds without number. Over five hundred creatures, and most of them are decoration.
b161795b0470578ec4d375341a2f109e111c8296.speaker: Narrator

3d27373c4824ebab98f4361171884cba09f5196c.text: And note where the borders end up. As the battle comes on, the fables stop. The lower border fills with severed heads, dropped shields, and men stripping mail off corpses — the salvage crew of history, working the margins while the story above stays heroic.
3d27373c4824ebab98f4361171884cba09f5196c.speaker: Narrator

00be9553cf1172194c3574269f166353b6ca4410.text: Clip four is the strangest object in the room. A woman stands in a doorway between two carved pillars. A tonsured churchman reaches in and touches — or strikes — her face. The caption reads: WHERE A CERTAIN CLERIC AND AELFGYVA. And then the cloth moves on and never mentions either of them again.
00be9553cf1172194c3574269f166353b6ca4410.speaker: Narrator

39e55fcbac4d7a81ce4440df1eec034fea40ef73.text: The honest list of candidates, all of them proposed, none of them established: Aelfgifu of Northampton, King Cnut's first wife, whose sons' paternity was gossip for a generation. Emma of Normandy, who took the name Aelfgifu in England. A sister of Harold, spoken of in a marriage bargain with a Norman. An abbess of Leominster and a Godwinson. Some scholars think the scene is scandal; some think it is a legal dispute over a woman's property; some think it is a joke about a churchman.
39e55fcbac4d7a81ce4440df1eec034fea40ef73.speaker: Narrator

a4a5cdc499a01ac3a9e5a772d39ce2cec6514366.text: This game will not tell you what happened to Aelfgyva, because nobody knows. What it will tell you is what the panel proves: an entire scandal, obvious enough to be sewn into a state document, can vanish so completely that only a woman's name survives it.
a4a5cdc499a01ac3a9e5a772d39ce2cec6514366.speaker: Narrator

bbf83e4072de93e0ac3a1c4569fa4f3b978b47c5.text: Clip five. The most reproduced image of the eleventh century, and the one people are surest about, and the one they should be least sure about.
bbf83e4072de93e0ac3a1c4569fa4f3b978b47c5.speaker: Narrator

5471bf276ecec26f33dfc5c31ee927f33fb85e49.text: HERE KING HAROLD WAS KILLED. The caption runs across TWO figures. One stands under the word HAROLD with a shaft at his helmet, hand up at his face. The next is being cut down by a mounted knight, a sword to the thigh.
5471bf276ecec26f33dfc5c31ee927f33fb85e49.speaker: Narrator

140fae138b531180142de8000f3099da2ebd6772.text: The written sources split the same way. The Norman writer closest to the battle says nothing about an eye. A chronicler some fifteen years later has the eye; another, thirty-odd years on, has the arrow. And blinding was the standard punishment for a perjurer — which makes an arrow in the oath-breaker's eye the tidiest ending the Norman case could possibly have.
140fae138b531180142de8000f3099da2ebd6772.speaker: Narrator

accba7a8b201b2672d148120a33f3381407b07f9.text: One more thing about this end of the cloth: it does not have an end. The linen stops mid-rout, with English foot running into the border. The final panel is lost — most reckon it showed the coronation. The last word of the conquest's own account of itself has gone missing, and everybody has been filling it in ever since.
accba7a8b201b2672d148120a33f3381407b07f9.speaker: Narrator

cd0e5670add97c2ebf86611347365b5ae9fe2286.text: Last clip, and it is not on the cloth. It is what happened TO the cloth — which is the same story the rest of this chapter tells, run at the speed of centuries.
cd0e5670add97c2ebf86611347365b5ae9fe2286.speaker: Narrator

ee6fb9abf870a14be5cf1f4e13821f3b88ea20d5.text: Eleven years later it is in Paris, on public display, while Napoleon assembles an army to invade England from the same coast. The star gets pointed at: a comet appeared in 1066, a comet had appeared again, and the exhibition is an argument with a queue. When the invasion is shelved, the cloth goes home.
ee6fb9abf870a14be5cf1f4e13821f3b88ea20d5.speaker: Narrator

88c5e7e86c47bc312e248a4009cc9d67b234042d.text: 1885 and 1886. In Leek, in Staffordshire, Elizabeth Wardle and some thirty-five needlewomen embroider a full-size replica from hand-coloured photographs — the whole seventy metres, again, by hand. It hangs in Reading to this day. They made one alteration: the naked figures were given drawers. The Victorians could copy a conquest and not a penis.
88c5e7e86c47bc312e248a4009cc9d67b234042d.speaker: Narrator

2c0cb6888f7627215930612f043c3f0f1ba0d437.text: Back to Bayeux after the war; in its own museum since 1983; on the UNESCO Memory of the World register since 2007. France announced in 2025 that it would lend the cloth to the British Museum while Bayeux rebuilds the gallery — which would put it back in the country that probably made it, for the first time in nine centuries.
2c0cb6888f7627215930612f043c3f0f1ba0d437.speaker: Narrator

3b718c2b8b52403bcf6cf72fd07e3b0cc4e8a2be.text: Twenty-one years, ten turnings of the screw. Choose an event and hear how it landed — on the king, on his lieutenant, on the rebels, on the chronicler, on the people who ploughed.
3b718c2b8b52403bcf6cf72fd07e3b0cc4e8a2be.speaker: Narrator

dec93644a4ef8b4b7736911945bef6fe0a15c72a.text: Ten events, twenty-one years, and not one of them experienced the same way twice. Pick a turning of the screw.
dec93644a4ef8b4b7736911945bef6fe0a15c72a.speaker: Narrator

1e6add9121a197fed9de4a463a074097d71f2eab.text: Twenty-one years in three movements: taking the country, burning it quiet, and writing it down so it can never argue again.
1e6add9121a197fed9de4a463a074097d71f2eab.speaker: Narrator

0f3ff7aef6e1dfe4cb903ce6b293a7067be9df2e.text: One autumn. A beach, a ridge, and a coronation that caught fire while the choir was still singing.
0f3ff7aef6e1dfe4cb903ce6b293a7067be9df2e.speaker: Narrator

128d7758180b98e00a2b371301ec9f302287216a.text: An order, a winter, and a spring where nothing came up. Three turnings, and the third one is only arithmetic — how many did not eat.
128d7758180b98e00a2b371301ec9f302287216a.speaker: Narrator

a6c5993c51aff0e5d08b602200a92c00539c38f0.text: Then the slow part. Stone on the high ground, a forest fenced against the men who lived in it, and a book that turns a country into a column of figures.
a6c5993c51aff0e5d08b602200a92c00539c38f0.speaker: Narrator

db078a58c53dd7b2d9155a2556000db4e5ad66f0.text: In one year he counts every plough in England and then makes every landholder in it swear to him personally. The two acts are the same act.
db078a58c53dd7b2d9155a2556000db4e5ad66f0.speaker: Narrator

6d8b978c069474b9a25a07d1f23fffb5e45a789a.text: So it is sorted. Two-handed arguments here, the long tail of policy there, and everything else in the index.
6d8b978c069474b9a25a07d1f23fffb5e45a789a.speaker: Narrator

66e55989bbd0f8e54404814fbfca9abd6355236b.text: Two reels with no choices in them. A winter, and a book. Watch. That is the whole instruction.
66e55989bbd0f8e54404814fbfca9abd6355236b.speaker: Narrator

214b2e4475c6937c4b374b1d14d00aa1276825ea.text: 1086. The commissioners reach the hundred court. Every man of the vill is sworn; the jurors are half English, half French; and a second panel will come behind this one to check its work.
214b2e4475c6937c4b374b1d14d00aa1276825ea.speaker: Narrator

948293be213859c0bf34af7dcbeb75d684be39e0.text: Historical note before anyone speaks: the inquest panels were barons, bishops and clerks deliberately sent into shires where they held no land, so that no man audited his own rents. Odo of Bayeux really did preside at the great plea on Penenden Heath. The stage gives him this bench too.
948293be213859c0bf34af7dcbeb75d684be39e0.speaker: Narrator

8bff54117ce5404d98d7d5125312bc391e0f7546.text: Domesday counted ploughs because ploughs were the medieval unit of productive capacity — the closest thing the eleventh century had to a machine-hours figure. Once a capacity is written down, it can be taxed whether or not it turns.
8bff54117ce5404d98d7d5125312bc391e0f7546.speaker: Narrator

fb5fe1ce3efb6fb0f806b3f526b4d4a56a718b89.text: Domesday records some six thousand mills in England. Within two centuries lords across Europe were suppressing hand-querns to force tenants to the seigneurial mill — the same logic, made explicit: own the bottleneck, and the harvest walks to you.
fb5fe1ce3efb6fb0f806b3f526b4d4a56a718b89.speaker: Narrator

012a794cc331dc9a89a48bef2b9491e5c16e1952.text: Woodland really was entered in Domesday as pannage for so many swine. Within a generation forest law would criminalize the same use it here merely prices — first the wood is assessed, then it is fenced.
012a794cc331dc9a89a48bef2b9491e5c16e1952.speaker: Narrator

6f07cebd9325054ac3af3bee634ea53d0e0037ad.text: Under-declaration was real and so were its penalties: the second panel existed precisely to catch it. Choose what the vill swears.
6f07cebd9325054ac3af3bee634ea53d0e0037ad.speaker: Narrator

e1cfeb1c0261ce9fa6d8381e792a24c327ecc206.text: The board stands at {geld} shillings. One hide of it does not exist. That gap — the difference between what a place is and what a book says it is — is the only room a village ever gets, and it closes a little every survey.
e1cfeb1c0261ce9fa6d8381e792a24c327ecc206.speaker: Narrator

e35b02e5085d2e1eb04647e911154fd45939a01c.text: The board stands at {geld} shillings, and every one of them is true. This is the chapter's hardest sentence: a completely honest survey is still a machine for taking things.
e35b02e5085d2e1eb04647e911154fd45939a01c.speaker: Narrator

2f5324254c7d4c577936b7bbe6d1e9a1ef561dd1.text: A fixed assessment turns every bad harvest into arrears. The book's permanence — its entire purpose — is exactly what made it merciless. Domesday entries were still being cited in English courts in the twentieth century.
2f5324254c7d4c577936b7bbe6d1e9a1ef561dd1.speaker: Narrator

62032b6aa2414c6f56a98e7ed7a6d4cd00106289.text: The dispute changed nothing and cost nothing, which is what makes it worth staging. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle is one long version of exactly this move: you cannot stop the entry, so you file the objection, and you keep the objection alive for nine hundred years.
62032b6aa2414c6f56a98e7ed7a6d4cd00106289.speaker: Narrator

3e0076c0b403f0ff687386ea39b4bba409ee32f7.text: A walking episode. Aldric leaves the vill on foot and keeps going. The pack holds three days of bread; the road holds whatever it holds.
3e0076c0b403f0ff687386ea39b4bba409ee32f7.speaker: Narrator

922e37b32aa3d4f562fd4d58d85d20b2ec7672bf.text: The road out of a burned country is not empty. It is the busiest place in England, and every person on it is going the same direction for the same reason.
922e37b32aa3d4f562fd4d58d85d20b2ec7672bf.speaker: Narrator

19ddc448afb330490b6387036add47db1ac0a80e.text: Open ground, no cover, and the wind doing the work the knights did not have to.
19ddc448afb330490b6387036add47db1ac0a80e.speaker: Narrator

c85e0232155c6902e836dab6c7619c51e2186bda.text: He gives away a third of the pack in eleven seconds, having thought about it for none of them. Charity on a famine road is not a virtue. It is a protocol.
c85e0232155c6902e836dab6c7619c51e2186bda.speaker: Narrator

56fddb3bd08e0e68703eba22441f8f79eaf24a93.text: A vill by the track, roofs intact, doors open, nobody in it. Not burned. Just left.
56fddb3bd08e0e68703eba22441f8f79eaf24a93.speaker: Narrator

5fa102eb86ea7fedd47ca01cb2df6197933277b3.text: Two horsemen pass at a walk, sixty yards off, looking at nothing. It takes a full minute. It is the longest minute in the episode and nothing whatever happens in it.
5fa102eb86ea7fedd47ca01cb2df6197933277b3.speaker: Narrator

1b64b3a18bfd9b98acb404d3370580389d757256.text: A sack goes over the tail-board anyway, because a carter is a man too and it is a long way to Durham. Nobody says anything. That is also documented behaviour, in the negative: the famine chronicles cannot explain how anyone at all survived.
1b64b3a18bfd9b98acb404d3370580389d757256.speaker: Narrator

049eaa0b2bba0017ade72a5592df61d0a5fe7ee2.text: The road runs under a raw motte, the timber still pale. There is no way round it. Roads go where castles are; that is the entire design.
049eaa0b2bba0017ade72a5592df61d0a5fe7ee2.speaker: Narrator

ad76d18c4bb2b23add41b0333b7f44aa48c247f4.text: Nobody stops him. The gate is manned, the men are bored, and a thin man walking south with a hoe is not a threat, an asset, or an entry.
ad76d18c4bb2b23add41b0333b7f44aa48c247f4.speaker: Narrator

c700cc26a9ffbb6dbb76f7b12e6b05d17632d22d.text: The country he is walking through was harried at RUTHLESSNESS {ruthless}. There is no relief here, no almonry, no abbey with stores — the columns came through and the abbeys gave out their grain in the first month.
c700cc26a9ffbb6dbb76f7b12e6b05d17632d22d.speaker: Narrator

79fa72e2f74f8984982157230db4a7cc7dc6ba9a.text: The harrying reached here in a thinner form: some stores intact, some vills paying, the machine already back at work collecting from the survivors.
79fa72e2f74f8984982157230db4a7cc7dc6ba9a.speaker: Narrator

6432320d23ebb6f0641b3e7fb5bcb028335e42f0.text: The order came late here and light, and it shows: byres standing, smoke from chimneys, and a reeve on the track counting people as they pass.
6432320d23ebb6f0641b3e7fb5bcb028335e42f0.speaker: Narrator

c97d76c2b53cf56740c874f00bb80642ebcc4e6e.text: Where the road gives up and the water starts. A man is standing in it to the knee, doing something to a net, and has clearly been watching the road for some time.
c97d76c2b53cf56740c874f00bb80642ebcc4e6e.speaker: Narrator

0cf12e71071fe1d9d681e6966cb197b78fe821d4.text: {roadMiles} miles, six days, one man, one hoe. The chronicles compress this into a clause. The clause took a week to walk.
0cf12e71071fe1d9d681e6966cb197b78fe821d4.speaker: Narrator

5f4b7c6792ce11fd185f0df07e4d1812173dd821.text: Behind him: a shire harried at RUTHLESSNESS {ruthless}, two-thirds of it still marked vasta in the king's own book seventeen years on.
5f4b7c6792ce11fd185f0df07e4d1812173dd821.speaker: Narrator

62aa1a11a92a7a6b2705e5e7c21235e3ff9c8715.text: Behind him: one granary the column passed by, and a country that otherwise burned exactly as scheduled. One exception does not make a policy. It makes a witness.
62aa1a11a92a7a6b2705e5e7c21235e3ff9c8715.speaker: Narrator

6eaf2090069b9a41a92daa1bc40229fde0c9a3e7.text: Behind him: a shire that burned whatever the king felt about it in the hall. The gauge reads {ruthless} and the smoke does not care.
6eaf2090069b9a41a92daa1bc40229fde0c9a3e7.speaker: Narrator

6a739074b5fbf377970f4a7689286bcbcf9bdd8c.text: Post-Conquest law spent the next two centuries closing exactly that gap — villeinage bound the tenant to the land and made leaving without licence an offence. He is right that it is the last free thing. He is early to notice, and the machine is already drafting.
6a739074b5fbf377970f4a7689286bcbcf9bdd8c.speaker: Narrator

976f738fd9e7415171135744403c4ed2d8d876bf.text: The commissioners ride out at noon. By evening the figure is at the cross, and a figure at a cross stops being a fact and starts being a career.
976f738fd9e7415171135744403c4ed2d8d876bf.speaker: Narrator

c08efaf66e44a4e23d38d25475ca4f8888044e6f.text: Two-thirds of Yorkshire was still returned as waste in 1086; the geld went out regardless. Note the mechanism, because it recurs in every chapter of this game: the machine's own records document its damage, and the records do not slow the collection by one day.
c08efaf66e44a4e23d38d25475ca4f8888044e6f.speaker: Narrator

9653cedd638af8e06cb6afe2e5aca896e525e381.text: Three hundreds over, at the end of a week, with ale in it. Watch a true number become a useful one.
9653cedd638af8e06cb6afe2e5aca896e525e381.speaker: Narrator

afbaab78476233228a3524ada894b8526cd71083.text: The true figure is {geld}. The travelling figure is {rumorGeld}. Both of them are now historical forces, and only one of them is a fact — which is the oldest problem in the trade and the reason this game shows its sources.
afbaab78476233228a3524ada894b8526cd71083.speaker: Narrator

b1bd5f194087841905f7d92d1ff0e9a311f17a5a.text: It takes eleven days for a village number to reach a king, and it arrives wearing a different coat.
b1bd5f194087841905f7d92d1ff0e9a311f17a5a.speaker: Narrator

239359189316f331c9f847b584e45350f231700c.text: Power owns the true number and the means to enforce it; everyone else owns the travelling one. Nine centuries later the asymmetry is unchanged, except that the travelling number now moves at the speed of light and the enforcement still moves at the speed of a sheriff.
239359189316f331c9f847b584e45350f231700c.speaker: Narrator

65763a2134db4d640d1ce6c13600a12036aeab73.text: Nobody else awake. A man with a stick, a floor, and a number he cannot make come out.
65763a2134db4d640d1ce6c13600a12036aeab73.speaker: Narrator

2be46fccabd53369551d033460a82626deeb8575.text: Henry George, eight hundred years downstream, in one sentence: rent takes the difference between what the land yields and what it costs to live. Aldric has just derived it at a hearth with a stick, because it is not a theory. It is what the evening actually feels like.
2be46fccabd53369551d033460a82626deeb8575.speaker: Narrator

e2d5a5be5efdc66b7d7693913188ba4fee48f402.text: Away from the hall and the fire. Three episodes at ground level: a bench where a village is written down, a road out of a burned country, and a number that leaves home and comes back a stranger.
e2d5a5be5efdc66b7d7693913188ba4fee48f402.speaker: Narrator

a89ad410164f877a383ed6d77362ba272b49f045.text: The chronicles are thin down here, so the sources get flagged as they arrive. What the record does hold at this altitude: plough-teams, mills, pannage for swine, and the word vasta, sixty times a page.
a89ad410164f877a383ed6d77362ba272b49f045.speaker: Narrator

7fa23533af7a0779ca007b8c1e3c85367d514b68.text: Night. The column reaches the village after dark, as ordered. Fire needs no daylight.
7fa23533af7a0779ca007b8c1e3c85367d514b68.speaker: Narrator

ddb9780a642b874b5b5a79795b2e79e0ece5272f.text: The granary first. They always know where the granary is.
ddb9780a642b874b5b5a79795b2e79e0ece5272f.speaker: Narrator

42a919efe5d1707186f25660942c4c934ca4ad6c.text: Then the byre. The cattle are driven out and killed in the lane — not stolen. Killed. Food is the target.
42a919efe5d1707186f25660942c4c934ca4ad6c.speaker: Narrator

7f64255994d4cd870252d7ad536337ae8d9c2a09.text: No one fights. The village walks into the dark with what it can carry, which is winter.
7f64255994d4cd870252d7ad536337ae8d9c2a09.speaker: Narrator

9061fdcfa2af89050c9ccc90eb5b4dbf6634563e.text: Symeon of Durham: 'Between York and Durham no village was inhabited. To the traveller there was only wasteness.'
9061fdcfa2af89050c9ccc90eb5b4dbf6634563e.speaker: Narrator

315644a66d86459f4181b2536561f4820001422a.text: Then it snows. It falls on the ash as it fell on the thatch, without opinion, and by morning the place is a white page.
315644a66d86459f4181b2536561f4820001422a.speaker: Narrator

33118a3f13f943997c7888db87ae46ded368bdb6.text: The ledger of what you watched. REPRESSION climbs toward its ceiling — the fires are the enforcement arm of the rent.
33118a3f13f943997c7888db87ae46ded368bdb6.speaker: Narrator

669945999e74ef4349954a4757de8447140594ca.text: FLARE-UPS climb with it. Burn a shire and every survivor is a future rising; repression manufactures its own demand.
669945999e74ef4349954a4757de8447140594ca.speaker: Narrator

33a99bf982b38800b80131bb7bce00d2053945f5.text: And THE MARGIN falls. The margin is the best land a free family can still work without paying a lord. Burn the free North, and there is nowhere left to stand outside the system.
33a99bf982b38800b80131bb7bce00d2053945f5.speaker: Narrator

3c5f9522a1613ce89b5a0bc5ba883cfbbc283323.text: Henry George, eight centuries early: when the margin falls, wages fall with it — everywhere, for everyone. Rent captures the difference. That is what the fire was for.
3c5f9522a1613ce89b5a0bc5ba883cfbbc283323.speaker: Narrator

76323d7c03561875e67659fe72d503df30675d41.text: No fire tonight. Candles, and the sound of quills. This is the other weapon.
76323d7c03561875e67659fe72d503df30675d41.speaker: Narrator

21158747e85a3b3454bc4ea450279f9eadbe46cb.text: Every hide, every holder, every ox, every mill, every man. The scratching does not stop for weather, mourning, or memory.
21158747e85a3b3454bc4ea450279f9eadbe46cb.speaker: Narrator

ff96bd739037e472853acc1af543ac93a8b41171.text: A clerk reaches a Yorkshire entry. A village. It had six families, two ploughs, a mill. It had a name; it still has a name — names are free.
ff96bd739037e472853acc1af543ac93a8b41171.speaker: Narrator

1ee1ba265fbd10a5214bf4cdf16a8e55e28cde8f.text: Then the value, as the commissioners found it, seventeen years after the fires.
1ee1ba265fbd10a5214bf4cdf16a8e55e28cde8f.speaker: Narrator

16c2b677381f11e62bf348a87e81617fe7c83977.text: Vasta. Waste. One word, sixty times a page, in the neatest hand in Europe.
16c2b677381f11e62bf348a87e81617fe7c83977.speaker: Narrator

52c1cd5a46bd781fcf04bb61551ad5aaaa5d961f.text: The torch did the taking. The Book does the keeping: every field valued, entered, and owed — forever, to the number. This is what forever looks like written down.
52c1cd5a46bd781fcf04bb61551ad5aaaa5d961f.speaker: Narrator

bfc6e195ea01ae2f8d52fcdd5fed822f1c7035c9.text: The ledger of what you watched. GREED climbs — not appetite, but appetite made permanent: every acre assessed at what it might yield, and taxed to the assessment, drought or no.
bfc6e195ea01ae2f8d52fcdd5fed822f1c7035c9.speaker: Narrator

7cc1aa629ecf25b2796568341099720524d9689b.text: THE MARGIN falls again, and this time on parchment. When the Book says there is no free land, there is no free land — the record outranks the soil.
7cc1aa629ecf25b2796568341099720524d9689b.speaker: Narrator

b5657202ac8ce1f2064622bb9ae5fa99af3c2c8f.text: And REPRESSION barely needs to move. That is the pen's discount: a survey collects what a garrison collects, at a fraction of the knights.
b5657202ac8ce1f2064622bb9ae5fa99af3c2c8f.speaker: Narrator

13b4b7be21a5a9d68201896c9759d15c26c36abb.text: George's law holds on vellum as on ash: rent captures the difference between the best land and the margin. Fix the margin in a book, and you fix wages everywhere — downward, forever.
13b4b7be21a5a9d68201896c9759d15c26c36abb.speaker: Narrator
